page: Amazon Web Services m8id.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU is equipped with 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The instance includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It is equipped with 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, running on the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core Geekbench, Passmark CPU, and Passmark database operations, alongside top-tier memory bandwidth for both small and large block read-only operations. It also demonstrates top-tier throughput in static web serving and Redis SET operations, reaching 169.45 million operations per second. However, a performance tradeoff is visible between single-core and multi-core execution; while multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores rank in the top 25% and top 10% respectively, single-core stress-ng performance sits in the average category.

The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning acceleration. In LLM inference benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models. However, text generation speeds show a relative decline, dropping to average for small and large models, though remaining strong for medium models. This profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for high-density multi-threaded workloads, database hosting, and software compilation, where its massive L3 cache and DDR5 memory bandwidth can be fully utilized.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and 384.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, running on the Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor at 3.9 GHz with 480 MB of L3 cache, it integrates 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 40 Gbps baseline network. Benchmarks reveal top-tier multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and memory read bandwidth, though single-core performance remains average. The hardware supports AVX-512 and AMX extensions, delivering top-tier LLM prompt processing speeds, though text generation speeds are more moderate. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed local storage, this instance is optimized for multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and data-intensive general-purpose workloads.
